title: Library and asset stock-taking before the long break
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on conducting a thorough library and asset stock-take before the long holiday, protecting school resources and planning for next year.
body:
School libraries and general assets — furniture, equipment, laboratory materials, sports gear — gradually lose track of their own numbers without a periodic, deliberate stock-take. The long holiday period, with students and most activity paused, is the ideal window for this exercise, yet it is frequently skipped in the rush to close the term.

Why stock-taking matters beyond simple record-keeping

An accurate asset register is not just an administrative nicety — it informs next year's budget planning (what genuinely needs replacement versus what is assumed to need replacement), supports insurance claims if theft or damage occurs, and provides the documentation increasingly expected during MOE and TSC audits.

Library stock-take essentials

  • Physical count of books against the library register, identifying missing or damaged items
  • Outstanding student loans reconciled before students depart, not assumed to be resolved
  • Identification of subject areas or CBE pathways where the library collection is genuinely under-resourced relative to curriculum needs
  • A damaged or outdated materials list for potential disposal or replacement

Practical tip: Reconcile library loans before students leave for the holiday, not after. Once students have dispersed, recovering outstanding books becomes considerably harder, and the opportunity to address it directly is lost.

General asset stock-take

  • Furniture — desks, chairs, dormitory beds — counted and condition assessed
  • Laboratory equipment inventoried, particularly for STEM pathway practical subjects
  • Sports and co-curricular equipment accounted for and condition noted
  • ICT equipment — computers, projectors, any digital teaching tools — checked for functionality and security

Building the stock-take into budget planning

A stock-take completed in good time directly informs the budget planning process covered in our guide on planning next year's budget — replacement and acquisition needs identified through an actual count are far more defensible to a BOM than estimates made without a current inventory.

Making it a routine practice, not an annual crisis

Schools that conduct a brief interim stock review mid-year, in addition to the full holiday stock-take, catch discrepancies or losses earlier, when they are easier to investigate and address, rather than discovering a significant gap only once a year.
